items.title: Samsung Messages could soon find, send, and forward texts for you
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung Messages version 16.3.27.7 is rolling out in South Korea with groundwork for hands-free message management. 
 The update also hints at smarter message searches and the ability to check how received photos were created or edited. 
 Similar capabilities were spotted in China in September, but global versions of Samsung Messages still lack these additions. 

Samsung may have shut down its Messages app in the US in July , but that hasn’t stopped the company from developing new features for users elsewhere. The latest update rolling out in South Korea suggests Samsung is preparing its texting app for a future where AI assistants can do much more than help you write messages.

As Sam Updater spotted, Samsung Messages version 16.3.27.7 introduces support for 10 functions that AI assistants such as Gemini could use to interact directly with the app. These include drafting, sending, replying to, forwarding, searching for, and deleting messages, as well as looking up contacts.
items.t: Samsung Messages could soon find, send, and forward texts for you

items.title: Android just had one of its worst quarters, and Apple is benefiting
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Android accounted for 74% of global smartphone sales in Q3 2026, down five points from a year ago and its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, per Counterpoint Research. 
 iOS climbed to a record Q3 share of 21% as iPhone sales grew year-on-year, even as the overall market shrank 16%. 
 HarmonyOS held at 5% globally and took 22% of China’s market, with HUAWEI growing 12% while China’s market shrank 10%. 

The memory shortage has been dragging down phone sales all year, and new data shows it may be hurting Android more than its rivals.

According to Counterpoint Research , global smartphone sales fell 16% year-on-year in Q3 2026, a sharper drop than the 11% decline seen in Q2. Android’s share of those sales slipped to 74%, down from 79% in Q3 2025. That’s the lowest share Android has ever posted in a third quarter, though it’s still a touch above the 72% it hit in Q4 2025, when new iPhones typically give Apple a seasonal bump.
items.t: Android just had one of its worst quarters, and Apple is benefiting

OnePlus is exploring wider availability of its native Phone app and plans to bring OPPO’s Calendar app to its devices.

The transition from OxygenOS to ColorOS has brought plenty of changes to OnePlus phones. And while many of our readers have warmed up to the new software , not everything has been well received by fans. From missing features to the future of native OnePlus apps, the company has now addressed some of the biggest questions surrounding ColorOS 17, revealing what users can expect from future updates and what’s already gone for good.

In a recent AMA on the OnePlus Community forum , OnePlus revealed that it’s exploring plans to bring its native dialer to more markets. Many OnePlus phones ship with Google Phone, while users in markets like India have access to the company’s own calling app, complete with features such as call recording without an audible announcement, AI-powered call summaries, and real-time translations . More users could eventually ditch Google’s dialer, although availability, including call recording support, will depend on the device and region.

items.title: Exclusive: Samsung is working on a private cloud for Galaxy AI, and it could look a lot like Apple’s
items.summary:
Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 points to “SPAC,” a new Samsung framework for processing AI requests on its servers while keeping them private. 
 SPAC appears to closely follow Apple’s Private Cloud Compute blueprint, and the code references AI models like Google’s Gemma 4 and Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6. 
 SPAC doesn’t seem to be active on the Galaxy S26 Ultra yet, and Samsung hasn’t announced it either. 

Galaxy AI has always made you choose between privacy and capability. Features that run on your phone keep your data there. However, the more capable ones, like Writing assist, Note assist, and generative photo edits, send your data to Samsung’s servers. Samsung’s current promise for those is a policy one: Photo Editor, for instance, tells you your image “will be sent to servers for processing… but not stored by Samsung.” If you’d rather not take that on trust and face value , the only option is the “Process data only on device” toggle in Galaxy AI Settings, which switches those cloud-based features off entirely.

Apple pitched a way around that trade-off two years ago when it launched Private Cloud Compute with Apple Intelligence in iOS 18. Private Cloud Compute (PCC) promises to extend device-level privacy to server-side AI processing: your request still goes to a server, but it’s encrypted, anonymized, and processed in a way that even Apple says it can’t access. Google and Meta have since built their own versions, with Google promising your personal data stays private to you and is not accessible to anyone else, “not even Google.”…
items.t: Exclusive: Samsung is working on a private cloud for Galaxy AI, and it could look a lot like Apple’s

We reviewed dozens of products in 2026 , and the one through line across all of them was cost. Because of RAMageddon, everything was more expensive, and it became somewhat easier to separate the products that were good because they were cheap from the ones that were good at any price.

This year was a lot of things, but it was primarily a reminder that the best products are created through careful iteration. Only one product on this list, the XREAL Aura, represents an emerging class. The rest, from the Fitbit Air to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, showcase years of work in optimizing for design, weight, battery life, and performance. Some take more risks than others, but to us they all represent the very best of their respective categories.

items.title: Save serious money with RedPocket Mobile’s $5 Black Friday plans
items.summary:
You’re not going to believe this, but there’s one part of your life that’s not actually getting more expensive. If you switch to RedPocket Mobile during its Black Friday sale, you can ditch your costly carrier and get a plan that starts at $5 per month. It’s not too good to be true: RedPocket has been around for 20 years, and unlike most MVNOs, it’s independently owned and operated. That gives it the ability to offer you real network choice when you sign up for a new plan (we’ll explain more later), and keeps your costs low. Really low.
